items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: My brother was writing. And he added Don Redman, because he had Don Redman under contract, so Don was getting like a hundred dollars off me, you know.

ctx.x: Oh yeah! Yeah, he... Well, it's a funny sort of thing, you know. Well, we went to do that Cotton Picker thing, and then the next thing you know, that folded. And when that folded, Joe, Prince, Clyde, they went with Blanche Calloway, and left me.

And I tried to get Joe to ...(? )...(? )... I was working with Zutty at Ryan's, and then I had to leave one day. They called me... Yeah, they used to call Joe "Don"(? ). He said, "Don(?) wants to go to California with me." I just said, "Well, what can I say? If he wants to go, you know..." ...[INAUDIBLE SENTENCE]... I had a gig for him, but he preferred to go to California. That kind of split the thing up, you know.

items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: the guy, old McDonald I called him, he just caught me and give me this. That meant two waltzes and two tangos!

ctx.x: Then one night I was just feeling like a little let down, you know, and I said, "Shit." So I played "Whispering" with the soft mute, you know, nice tempo, and the boss comes and said, "That's it." He said, "Now, if you play numbers like that, that's what people can consistently dance on. You know, later on... You can't just play that Jazz straight through." So from then on, I knew how to play it, you know.

Then on Sunday, we had one set where we could play anything we wanted, and then went hog wild for that one set. Near the end of the set, the guy, old McDonald I called him, he just caught me and give me this. That meant two waltzes and two tangos! That was the end of the Swing!
And we got air time down there, too; again, we got air time, you know. That was a good band, though. Don made some helluva arrangements on that band. Pshew! I just wish I had that book again.
